import struct

with open('/app/code.png', 'rb') as f:
    data = f.read()

# Skip PNG signature
i = 8
text_data = []
while i < len(data) - 12:
    length = struct.unpack('>I', data[i:i+4])[0]
    chunk_type = data[i+4:i+8].decode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    chunk_data = data[i+8:i+8+length]
    
    if chunk_type == 'tEXt':
        try:
            null_pos = chunk_data.index(b'\x00')
            key = chunk_data[:null_pos].decode('latin-1')
            value = chunk_data[null_pos+1:].decode('latin-1')
            text_data.append((key, value))
            print(f"tEXt: {key} = {value}")
        except:
            pass
    elif chunk_type == 'iTXt':
        print(f"iTXt chunk found (length={length})")
    elif chunk_type == 'zTXt':
        print(f"zTXt chunk found (length={length})")
    
    i += 12 + length

print(f"\nFound {len(text_data)} text chunks")
EOF

import hashlib

# Read the image
with open('/app/code.png', 'rb') as f:
    img_bytes = f.read()

# h0 = SHA256(img_bytes)
h0 = hashlib.sha256(img_bytes).digest()

# SALT = "0000TBENCH-SALT"
SALT = "0000TBENCH-SALT"

# H = SHA256(h0 || h0[:10] || SALT)
# This matches the pseudocode interpretation:
# - h0 is the full hash of the image
# - h0[:10] is the first 10 bytes (from "hof:10]" which meant h0[0:10])
# - SALT is the salt string

input_data = h0 + h0[:10] + SALT.encode()
H = hashlib.sha256(input_data)

# Get hex representation
result = H.hexdigest()

print(f"Result: {result}")
print(f"First 6 chars: {result[:6]}")

# Verify it starts with bee26a as per the hint
assert result.startswith("bee26a"), f"Expected to start with 'bee26a', got '{result[:6]}'"
print("Verification passed!")

# Write to output file
with open('/app/output.txt', 'w') as f:
    f.write(result)

print("\nWritten to /app/output.txt:")
with open('/app/output.txt', 'r') as f:
    print(f.read())
EOF
